Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
729 AM EDT Wed Sep 16 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 248 AM EDT Wednesday...

For Friday, wind gusts have increased and humidity has 
decreased for most locations.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 248 AM EDT Wednesday...

1. Afternoon/evening showers remain likely for portions of the 
region Thursday followed by breezy and drier weather for Friday.


2. Below normal temperatures and moisture to start the weekend 
will support chances for patchy to potentially widespread frost 
in portions of northern New York and central/eastern Vermont.

3. Cooler weather with chance for precipitation Saturday night 
into Sunday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 248 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Following the passage of decaying front today, 
the old boundary will be positioned just to our south tomorrow 
as a wave of low pressure develops. Meanwhile, another cold 
front to our northwest will be approaching. The combination of 
large scale lift ahead of this front and the moisture advection 
from the system south of the region appears to help blossom rain
over our region during the afternoon, generally expanding 
towards the north and east with time. Model spread continues to 
be large with regards to the exact footprint of the rain, still 
favoring our southern Vermont locales while rain chances become 
more questionable as you go northward. Increasing low level 
moisture will support some instability, but most guidance shows 
insufficient lapse rates to get deep convection and associated 
thunder. Still, slight chances of thunder statistically are 
warranted at this time over southern/eastern portions of the 
region during the late afternoon into the early evening before 
showers exit to our east.

Friday continues to look like a classic early fall day. 
Following a secondary cold front passing through early in the 
day, much drier, cool air will be evident. Have trended winds 
and wind gusts higher as guidance has consistently shown a gusty
northwest flow pattern that would allow widespread 30 MPH gusts
in much of northern Vermont, with slightly lighter winds in 
northern New York. There will be impressively dry air aloft to 
tap into such dew points will plummet during the morning as the 
boundary layer deepens. As a result, low humidity values can be 
expected in lower elevations especially, likely below 40% in the
Champlain Valley and Connecticut River Valley.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Following a breezy afternoon, cool high pressure
to our northwest may crest sufficiently overhead that winds 
slacken enough to allow for frost development, especially in 
most sheltered locations above 1000 feet elevation. The latest 
NBM 10th percentile low temperatures seems like a good first 
guess if radiational cooling is as efficient as it could be in 
this type of setup, showing temperatures cooling into the low to
mid 30s throughout the Adirondacks and central and eastern 
Vermont Saturday morning. Model output statistics for perennial 
cold spot at the Adirondack Regional Airport currently shows a 
low of 29, which is only a couple degrees lower than what was 
observed yesterday morning and seems reasonable. 

With light winds and a cooler start to the day, high 
temperatures Saturday will probably be near to slightly lower 
than on Friday. The air will remain crisp with dew points again 
mainly in the 30s during the day. Precipitable moisture will be 
quite low, as the ensemble mean values only gradually increase 
above 50% of normal from west to east as the air mass slightly 
modifies.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Still quite a bit of uncertainty with regards to
possibility of some rain showers Saturday night into Sunday. 
ECMWF has continued to keep our region drier with system 
remaining south of our region. GFS has now returned to a 
solution with our region having some light rain Saturday night 
and Sunday. Will hope for better model agreement as we get 
closer to the weekend. For now have chance for showers mentioned
from 06-18z Sunday. Weather pattern will remain active through 
next week with additional chances for showers on Tuesday and 
then again towards the end of the work week. Temperatures will 
start out cooler than normal this weekend then trend back 
towards seasonal normals by mid week.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 12Z Thursday...Showers have moved out of our region but
mid level clouds remain. Will have some breaks in the clouds 
this afternoon and ceiling heights will lift as well. Mainly a 
wind forecast for all sites with winds veering from southerly to
southwesterly, and eventually northwesterly. Will watch for fog
potential tonight, especially EFK. 

Outlook...

Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 227 AM EDT Wednesday...Channeled southerly flow remains 
in place early this morning, with winds between 15 and 25 knots 
on the north lake and broad waters of Lake Champlain along with 
significant wave heights between 2 and 3 feet. Conditions will 
improve through the morning as winds gradually weaken, and winds
will become light and variable this afternoon before turning 
northerly as a weak front passes through.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
